$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the unsupported PASS in its second form, and the harder one. No
threshold is invented here. The threshold is real and stated, and the run passes it on a sentence in the
tech spec asserting the service is well covered, which is a claim rather than a measurement. It then lists
no evidence gap, because a run that believes the claim has nothing to report.
Duplication moves to N/A in the same edit, because the domain status is the worst status in the section and
a CONCERNS left there would hold the domain at CONCERNS and hide the judgment this case is about.
derivation: Maintainability: PASS, N/A, PASS, PASS, and N/A never wins, so PASS against an expected CONCERNS. One status
miss and one unsupported PASS, on the domain the ground truth marks undecidable for missing evidence.
Thresholds: the section still names 80% in its coverage threshold line, so the check passes. All four pass.
Unknown threshold: the Performance section is untouched and still carries UNKNOWN, so the document-level
Evidence gaps: the list is empty, which is the reading this run committed to. On the gapped bundle an empty
list is not scored as a false positive; it is the maintainability status that carries the judgment.
Overall stays FAIL for the same reason as the previous case.
Citations: gapped-correct-audit's nineteen, unchanged. The Test Coverage line cites docs/tech-spec.md in both runs,
which is the point of the case: this run and the correct audit read one file and reach opposite answers from it, so
the grounding is identical and the judgment is the whole of what moved. The file is one the bundle carries, so
nothing is fabricated, and reading a real file as the wrong kind of evidence is a judgment error, counted apart
Coverage: four headings, four of them stating a readable status.
Duplicate sections: none. Every domain this report assesses has exactly one section.

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
